question: May cron auto-delivery silently discard a payload solely because its English prose resembles a narration of a send action?
rationale: Source inspection proves unavoidable false positives in the lexical classifier, but whether that message-loss tradeoff is acceptable is a delivery-policy choice rather than a routine implementation detail.

options.title: Require structured evidence
options.body: Suppress text only when run metadata proves it redundantly narrates an already-completed outbound action.

options.title: Accept lexical suppression
options.body: Land the heuristic with explicit ownership of occasional valid-message suppression and language-dependent behavior.

options.title: Use prompt guidance only
options.body: Keep the safer prompt improvement while declining delivery-layer suppression until a reliable signal exists.

recommendation.title: Require structured evidence
recommendation.body: Suppress text only when run metadata proves it redundantly narrates an already-completed outbound action.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work owns the adjacent direct-delivery and double-announce behavior where this policy would live.
